tagline: A desert loop beside wagon ruts and peaks named for racers.
intro: The Silver Island Mountain National Back Country Byway circles a desert range on a 54-mile loop near Wendover. The Bureau of Land Management gives two to three hours for the drive and highlights rocky terraces and historic wagon ruts. The range has the Bonneville Salt Flats along its southeast flank and Pilot Valley Playa to the west; Lake Bonneville's former shorelines terrace its slopes.

The loop gives access to the Hastings Cutoff of the California National Historic Trail, used by the Donner-Reed party in 1846. The party passed north of the range; Donner Canyon, in its northeast section, bears their name. Later travelers left different names: Tetzlaff Peak honors a driver who raced on the salt flats, and Graham Peak commemorates Athol Graham.

Approach from Interstate 80 at Exit 4 near Wendover, heading toward Leppy Pass and following the byway signs. The California Trail runs along the north end of the loop, where wagon-wheel ruts remain in the ground. Volcano Peak stands six miles northeast of Wendover, with Rishel Peak two miles farther northeast.
notice: Lake Bonneville shoreline terraces mark the slopes of the range.

moments.title: Tetzlaff Peak
moments.text: Tetzlaff Peak rises 2,000 feet above the Bonneville Salt Flats in a single mile. Its name recalls Teddy Tetzlaff, who drove a Blitzen Benz across the flats at 142.8 miles per hour on August 12, 1914. The U.S. Board on Geographic Names officially adopted the name in 1960. The 6,267-foot summit belongs to the Silver Island Mountains, with the Bonneville Speedway five miles to its southeast.

moments.title: California Trail
moments.text: Wagon-wheel ruts mark the California Trail along the north end of the byway. The modern loop provides access to the historic Hastings Cutoff, associated with the Donner-Reed party of 1846. That party passed north of the Silver Island Range, leaving its name on Donner Canyon in the northeast part of the mountains.
moments.notice: Wagon-wheel ruts survive along the California Trail at the north end of the loop.

moments.title: Volcano Peak
moments.text: Volcano Peak rises 1,800 feet above the Bonneville Salt Flats over a distance of 1.5 miles. The summit reaches 6,011 feet, with Wendover six miles to the southwest and Rishel Peak two miles to the northeast. Across the Silver Island Range, Lake Bonneville left terraces through shoreline erosion and deposition. The rocky slopes support sparse juniper, sagebrush, ricegrass and ephedra, and the range has no perennial streams.
